sections.kicker: Prepared for Srishti Chhabria by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Srishti's work has a point of view. The front page does not say it yet.
sections.keep: The gold DIRECTOR & PRODUCER headline on the dark page. It carries the weight of a film title card.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The headline names her job, not her work.
pins.why: Every director and producer can claim this headline. It does not say why her and not the next one.
pins.how: Say what kind of story she tells, in her own words.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: Anyone browsing sees a list of credits and no point of view.

pins.what: The film titles sit over bright stills, and the first one nearly disappears.
pins.why: The work is the pitch, and its names are the hardest thing on the screen to read.
pins.how: Give titles a steady place to sit that does not depend on the still behind them.
pins.label: Your titles
pins.cost: Visitors skim past the names of the films that should be remembered.

pins.what: A third tab holds the one signal no other director's site has.
pins.why: Advocacy tells us what her stories are for, and it sits last in the menu as a single word.
pins.how: Let the thread between the films and the advocacy show on the front page.
pins.label: Your menu
pins.cost: The reason to hire her over the next director stays one click away.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Srishti Chhabria. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and they point the same way.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Srishti Chhabria's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
